- When sentiment is consistently high (≥0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–3% for 30d horizon.
- After sharp sentiment spikes (≥1.00) followed by negative sentiment change, model often overshoots; apply downward correction of 2–5% in next 3–5 days.
- If news volume is high (≥2.0) and sentiment is neutral or negative, model overreacts; dampen forecast by 1–4% to align with true mean reversion.
- When true outcome shows strong mean reversion (e.g., 3–5 consecutive days of price decline after peak), model fails to adjust; reduce forecast by 2–5% for next 5–7 days.
- If model forecast is >10% above true outcome for 3 consecutive days, apply “lag correction”: subtract 0.5–1.5% per day until convergence.
- For 30d horizon, if sentiment history shows no clear trend (±0.33 change), model tends to overfit recent noise; use 30d moving average as baseline for correction.
- When sentiment turns negative (≤0.33) and news volume is low, model underestimates; add 1–3% to forecast to account for potential rebound.
- If model forecast is consistently below true outcome (by 2–4%) for 5+ days, model is underestimating mean; increase forecast by 1–3% for next 3–5 days.
